editorial.thesis: A learning-and-motor-trade city of about 247,000. Its retail is heavy on fitness & wellness and coaching & training, and thin on pharmacy & health retail and grocery & daily needs — and 49% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 39% of Guwahati's. 8.9 chain outlets per lakh residents against 22.73 in Guwahati; 9 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by KFC 6, Domino's 3, Pizza Hut 3.

The mapped economy leans to education. Shares of all mapped places: education 14.4% (Guwahati 9.0%); other services 11.6% (Guwahati 7.6%); shops & retail 10.8% (Guwahati 22.3%); food & beverage 5.7% (Guwahati 9.2%). Raw counts would mislead because Guwahati is mapped more completely (18,964 places against 1,297), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 3 zones hold 49% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Vaivakawn alone has about 46,000 residents and 3 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is less concentrated than in Guwahati. 52% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Guwahati 58%). The largest cores are Aizawl (309 places) and Chandmary (80).

The widest brand gaps against Guwahati. Domino's 3 outlets vs 30; Baskin Robbins 3 outlets vs 27; Apollo Pharmacy 0 outlets vs 22. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 6 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Guwahati, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Aizawl and Vaivakawn are the largest zones by residents (59,000 and 46,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 52% of all commercial places, and Aizawl alone lists 309.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Aizawl holds 11 of the 22 tracked chain outlets, and Chandmary adds 3.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Aizawl and Kulikawn lead on education places (51 and 17, with 8 and 5 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Vaivakawn and Kulikawn. The blue cores include Aizawl.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (18,964 places in Guwahati against 1,297 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Guwahati; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Guwahati, Aizawl's mapped places over-index on education (14.4% vs 9.0%), other services (11.6% vs 7.6%), automotive (5.8% vs 4.5%) and under-index on shops & retail (10.8% vs 22.3%), food & beverage (5.7% vs 9.2%), banks & finance (5.2% vs 6.7%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 22 outlets of 9 tracked national brands within 6 km — 8.9 per lakh residents against Guwahati's 22.73 (278 outlets of 35 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Guwahati are Domino's (3 vs 30); Baskin Robbins (3 vs 27); Apollo Pharmacy (0 vs 22). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Guwahati's, so low means thin by Guwahati's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 6 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Aizawl's age mix against Guwahati: children (0–14) 27.4% vs 20.5%, 15–24 21.0% vs 19.0%, working age 44.9% vs 53.5%, 60+ 6.7% vs 7.0%. Under-25s are 48% of residents.

zones.796001: A commercial core: 309 mapped places and 11 chain outlets (50% of the city's tracked chains) for about 59,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.
zones.796009: An under-served zone: about 46,000 residents, 45 mapped places, 3 food & drink and 2 chain outlets. Depth index 32.
zones.796005: An under-served zone: about 37,000 residents, 58 mapped places, 2 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 51.
zones.796017: An under-served zone: about 24,000 residents, 27 mapped places, 4 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 37.
zones.796007: Reasonably supplied: 80 places for about 24,000 residents (index 111), 3 chain outlets.
zones.796012: A student-and-family belt: 14 education places (2 coaching) and 7 healthcare places for about 19,000 residents, with 5 food & drink places and 1 chain outlets.
zones.796014: A commercial core: 58 mapped places and 3 chain outlets (14% of the city's tracked chains) for about 10,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 4.0% of mapped places against 6.9% in Guwahati — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: KFC 6 (Guwahati 24), Domino's 3 (Guwahati 30), Pizza Hut 3 (Guwahati 11). No mapped outlet in either city: Haldiram's, Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 1.9% of mapped places against 2.1% in Guwahati, so the mix is level. No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Point, Blue Tokai, Third Wave Coffee.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.3% of mapped places against 0.6% in Guwahati — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 3 (Guwahati 27). No mapped outlet in either city: Havmor, Naturals, Theobroma, Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 0.8% of mapped places against 3.7% in Guwahati — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: DMart 1 (Guwahati 7), Vishal Mega Mart 1 (Guwahati 6). No mapped outlet in either city: More, Easyday, Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.3% of mapped places against 2.0% in Guwahati — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: MedPlus, Wellness Forever.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 2.5% of mapped places against 6.0% in Guwahati — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 3 (Guwahati 21), Westside 1 (Guwahati 3), Titan 1 (Guwahati 12). No mapped outlet in either city: Shoppers Stop.
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 5.2% of mapped places against 6.7% in Guwahati — below its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.7% in Guwahati, so the mix is level.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.6% of mapped places against 3.6% in Guwahati, so the mix is level.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
